audit.whatIsWrong: full phases read Ahri, Ahri, Ahri, Skill, Skill, Ryze, Ryze while content win[] and the packet levelChart both read Ahri on all seven rows.
audit.why: The full layer handed Ryze the last two rows outright and called 4-6 even. Ahri is at 56.63% over 2859 games and the packet chart has no Ryze row anywhere. Worse, the full layer's own why text on those rows ("Late Ahri is a pick machine") argued for Ahri while the side said Ryze — the page disagreed with itself inside a single row.
audit.corrected: phases[3..6].side set to Ahri as one atomic group, matching win[3..6]; ratings normalised and the two rows whose why text no longer fitted rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: The root was attributed to E throughout ("Q into E-root", "a whiffed E leaves him with no follow-up", "the EQ chain"), and the actual conditional was never stated.
audit.why: Rune Prison is his W, 615 range, 11 seconds at rank 1 — and Riot's text is explicit: it damages and SLOWS, and roots only if the target already has Flux on them. Spell Flux (E) is the debuff that upgrades it, on a 3.5-second cooldown at 615 range. So the whole matchup has a clean break point that the page never named: deny Spell Flux and the root is only a slow. Naming the wrong slot meant a reader watching his E cooldown was watching a 3.5-second spell instead of the 11-second one that actually locks them down.
audit.corrected: Every reference rebuilt as Spell Flux into Rune Prison, with the conditional root stated in whys[1], wants.you[1], wants.foe[1], spikes[0], breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and whys[4] described a "root-Q-flash-ult combo" and "his R portal engage"; whys[0] and early said Ryze is "stuck auto-attacking for chip damage" at levels 1-2.
audit.why: Realm Warp creates a portal that teleports allies standing near it to the target location after a few seconds — 3000 range, 180 seconds at rank 1. It is a map and rotation tool, not an engage he flashes in with, and telling a player to fear it in a lane all-in points their attention at the wrong thing. And Overload is a 1000-range spell on a flat 5-second cooldown that his other abilities reset — he is not reduced to auto-attacks at any point in the game, he simply outranges your orb by 30 units while lacking the range to root you.
audit.corrected: Realm Warp described as the delayed group portal it is; the early-game description rebuilt on the 1000 vs 615 range split rather than on a false lack of poke.

notes: The root was attributed to Ryze's E across the whole matchup. It is Rune Prison (W, 615 range, 11s), and Riot's text makes it conditional: it SLOWS, and only roots a target that already carries Flux from Spell Flux (E, 3.5s). That conditional is the entire matchup and it appeared nowhere — a reader was being told to track the wrong slot and the wrong cooldown. Also corrected: Realm Warp described as an engage Ryze 'lands' on you, when it is a delayed 3000-range group portal; and the claim that Ryze is 'stuck auto-attacking for chip damage' early, when Overload is a 1000-range spell on a flat 5s cooldown that his other abilities reset. Level chart disagreed on four rows, and on two of them the full layer's side (Ryze) contradicted its OWN why text (which described Ahri winning). wants.you and wants.foe were each missing a fourth entry; both filled. Not asserted: whether Charm is cleansable or tenacity-reduced, and whether Rune Prison's root can be shortened by tenacity where the slow cannot.
